newsitem.title: CHINA: HK dollar seen stable, swap rates firming.
newsitem.headline: HK dollar seen stable, swap rates firming.

text.p: The Hong Kong dollar is expected to be stable and swap rates to firm after the currency re-opened notably stronger on Tuesday versus the weaker levels tested on Friday, dealers said.
Hong Kong markets were closed Monday for a holiday.
Traders said the local unit would be buoyed by Hong Kong people's confidence in the currency and high forward rates.

"Today it should not break over 7.75 mainly because forwards are too expensive for speculators to speculate on the Hong Kong dollar," said Meryl Phang, manager of financial analysis at Standard & Poor's MMS International.
The local currency stood at HK$7.7410/20 per dollar in early Tuesday, slightly down from HK$7.7404/14 at Monday's overseas closing.
It touched the key support level of HK$7.75 in London on Friday.
The Hong Kong dollar, the last major Asian curency linked to the U.S. dollar, has been pegged at HK$7.8 to US$1.00 since 1983 and is permitted to float in a narrow range around that level.
It has traded at around HK$7.74 this year.

"I think the Hong Kong dollar will be stable in Asia. I don't believe there's any panic. Hong Kong people have never panicked about the local currency. They are quite confident in it," said a dealer with an U.S. bank.
He attributed the Friday fall to overseas speculation.
He added the market could see commercial buying interest at HK$7.74.
The one-year swap rate was quoted at HK$7.75/8.25 and the six-month rate was quoted at HK$8.00/8.50.
Hang Seng Bank quoted the overnight interbank rate from 10 percent to 12 percent.

"Forward rates should still be under pressure to rise. So if corporate investors need Hong Kong dollars, they need to get it from the spot market," Phang said, tipping one-year forwards to trade at about HK$7.76.
She said the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the de facto central bank, would refrain from depositing money into the market to hold the interbank rate firm.
